 Judgment

This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.2256/2015 dated 07.12.2018 on the file of the XVIII Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & MACT, Bengaluru, seeking enhancement of the compensation and also questioning the contributory negligence fixed at 40% on the claimant.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The case of the claimant is that on 26.06.2014 at about 4.30 p.m. when the claimant was riding his motor cycle on Hebbal ring road, at that time a Tata Ace going with a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied break without giving any signal and stopped.
Due to which he dashed the TATA Ace from NC: 2023:KHC:45952 behind, as a result he sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
According to the claimant he is working as a labourer and earning an amount of Rs.18,000/- per month.
According to the doctor he had sustained 80% disability to the limb and 62% disability to the whole body.

The court below had observed that the RW-1 drove the Tata Ace vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and all of sudden, as the front vehicle slowed down by applying the break, he also suddenly slowed the vehicle and applied the break and hit Tata Ace.

The court below observed that it is the duty of the claimant to maintain the gap between the front vehicle and his vehicle as per traffic rules, but he was not diligent in doing so and for that reason, the accident had occurred.
Admittedly the Tata Ace vehicle is wide and heavy vehicle, the driver can see the vehicle moving ahead, but motor cycle is a light vehicle, it is difficult to observe the same.
In this case, admittedly the Tata Ace vehicle is proceeding ahead of the motor cycle, since the said vehicle applied sudden break, the claimant hit the Tata Ace vehicle.

Hence, the court has come to the NC:
2023:KHC:45952 conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of driver of the Tata Ace as well as the claimant and apportioned it on 40% on the claimant and 60% on the driver of the offending vehicle.
When it comes to the pain and suffering, the claimant has succumbed fracture of supra condylar left femur, fracture of left tibia and fibula, fracture of left clavicle and other injuries.
Operations were done, implants were removed on 05.11.2015.
Wound debridement was done for left leg, amputation above knee was done and discharged on 14.11.2015.

Again he was admitted to Christian Medical Hospital, Vellore on 26.09.2016, during that period, total wrist fusion left side Mr. Parveez Ahmed vs The Managing Director on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141554745/
2 done and discharged on 01.10.2016 with an advise to take further treatment.

sentences.text: He took treatment as inpatient for a period of 146 days, considering all these, under the head of pain and suffering the court below granted an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-, then coming to the medical expenses an amount of Rs.5,34,000/- was granted, towards loss of income during the laid up period, the court had taken income at Rs.9,000/- for 6 months had granted an amount NC: 2023:KHC:45952 of Rs.54,000/-.
When it comes to disability, the doctor had opined that 62% to the whole body, but the court below had taken 40% and granted compensation of an amount of Rs.7,34,400/-.

Towards food,
nourishment and attendant charges an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is granted, towards loss of future amenities an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is granted and towards future medical expenses an amount of Rs.65,000/- is granted.
Altogether compensation of an amount of Rs.16,87,400/- is awarded by the Tribunal.

As the contributory negligence is fixed at 60% on the driver of the offending vehicle,
insurance company was directed to pay an amount of Rs.10,13,000/- to the claimant.
3. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that in case of contributory negligence, it is for the Respondent to prove that there is contributory negligence.
In this case, the court below without any evidence had held that there is contributory negligence.
He submits that when the doctor has opined that he has sustained 62% disability NC: 2023:KHC:45952 to the whole body, the court below had taken 40% disability.
He submits that the court had not considered the future prospects.
He submits that in fact it is a case of 100% disability as he was not able to do his work.
Further on the other heads also, the compensation granted by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the court below had elaborately discussed about the nature of accident and role played by each of the driver and had rightly come to the conclusion that the contributory negligence is at 40% and 60%.
He submits that as far as the compensation awarded is just and reasonable and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.

Considering the amputation and injuries sustained by the claimant, under the head of pain and suffering, the court below NC: 2023:KHC:45952 had granted an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- which is a reasonable amount.
Towards medical expenses also, basing on the evidence, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.5,34,000/- and no interference is called for.
Coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, he was in hospital for 146 days, the court below had granted only for a period of 6 months.
Considering the period of recovery, this court is inclined to take 9 months, it comes to an amount of Rs.81,000/-.

Then coming to the disability, it is the case of amputation above the knee, he is a coolie, considering the occupation and the evidence of the doctor who deposed that the disability at 62% to the whole body.
This court is inclined to take 62% and income is taken as Rs.9,000/-, 40% of future prospects would come to Rs.3,600/-.

(Rs.9,000/- +Rs.3,600/-
=Rs.12,600/-) Under the head of loss of income due to disability an amount of Rs.15,93,648/- is granted.

Under the head of loss of future amenities, future medical expenses the amounts NC: 2023:KHC:45952 granted by the court below at Rs.1,00,000/- and Rs.65,000/- respectively are reasonable and no interference is called for.

Then coming to the contributory negligence, the court below had considering the sketch and the fact that the both the vehicles are moving one after the other, as Tata ace vehicle had applied the break and the claimant had dashed to the said vehicle, he fell down and sustained injuries.
Argument of learned counsel for the appellant that there is no contributory negligence cannot be accepted.
While proceeding on high way they have to maintain the minimum distance between the vehicle.
If he had maintained the distance, even if a sudden break is applied because of the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, accident could have been avoided.
The court below had rightly held that there is contributory - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:45952 negligence.

However coming to the apportionment of the contributory negligence, apportioning at 40% is on the higher side, this court is reducing the same to 20% on the claimant and 80% on the insurance company i.e, 80%, of Rs.24,83,648/- is Rs.19,86,918/-.
The insurance company is liable to pay an amount of Rs.19,86,918/- at 6% interest.
